From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Initial incident landing report: PioneerHealth degraded latency (4/20)

Team —

TL;DR: On 2028-04-20 02:07 UTC we experienced a service degradation affecting generation latency for the US region for ~58 minutes. Root cause: a misrouted rollout binary caused cache population regressions leading to elevated tail latency on the dedicated pool serving PioneerHealth traffic. Impact: several PioneerHealth request paths exceeded their SLO (99th percentile) and three customer-visible errors were raised. No data exfiltration.

Attachments: 2028-04-20_pioneer-postmortem.pdf, slo-timeline-20280420.csv

Key timeline (high level):
- 02:07 UTC: error rate and 99p latency spike detected by SLO monitor
- 02:12 UTC: automated routing fallback triggered; partial mitigation but elevated latency remained
- 02:35 UTC: on-call escalated to infra lead; rollback of rollout binary initiated
- 03:05 UTC: rollback completed; metrics normalized by 03:25 UTC

Proposed immediate action items (owners assigned in attached action register):
1) Short term: revert/replay pipeline hardening (owner: Markus Klein) — due 2028-04-25
2) Medium term: add pre-deploy cache-warm smoke tests for large sequence models (owner: Marissa Cole) — P0 for Q2
3) Customer comms: finalize postmortem and SLA credit calculation (owner: Hannah Schmitt) — deliver to CS by 2028-04-21

Notes for execs: SLA exposure estimate is ~0.9% of monthly committed tokens for PioneerHealth's Dedicated pool; legal and finance are being looped for any crediting. Full postmortem attached.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

What we fixed immediately: rollback of the problematic rollout binary and an automated fallback to reduce blast radius for future rollouts.

Planned mitigations (timelines):
- Rollout pipeline hardening (Markus) — code merged 2028-04-24, tests 2028-04-25

Apologies again for the disruption — we take this seriously and have already started delivering the fixes.

Best,
